<reason>Both sides were sharp and stayed on the motion, and the debate narrowed cleanly to one question: does "legal only when" actually bite. A built a coherent case (relocation under bans, deregulation harms, destination-state recognition as leverage, and a strong closing timing frame: only entry conditions arrive before irreversible harm). B, however, did more damaging offensive work. B's "enforced by whom / certificate as brochure" frame, the adoption turn (volumes collapsed rather than compliant channels flourishing), and above all the pressure-question dilemma forced A to choose between stranding infants and having a merely advisory mechanism. A answered honestly (A4.1: the child gets parentage anyway; the penalty is friction and litigation), but that concession was exactly what B needed, and B converted it in Rebuttal 2 and closing into a clean comparative: protections are selective (compliant lane only), legitimation is universal, so volume flows to the women most at risk. Critically, A never engaged the legitimation/market-expansion mechanism at any point, nor B's "escrow released on live birth is the same leverage in a nicer envelope." B, by contrast, did answer A's best pressure — distinguishing forward-looking permission plus safe harbour from backward-looking liability, and offering immunity plus medical care for the surrogate — even if that answer leaves B's own regime somewhat underspecified (legal-but-liable vs prohibited), which A exploited effectively with "the motion under another name or the relocation." That residual ambiguity, plus B overrunning the word cap three times, keeps the margin narrow rather than solid. On net B was more responsive to the decisive clash and left the cleaner reason to vote.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Pressure Q1 and follow-up: forcing A to say whether Germany refuses recognition in the cheap-Cambodian-clinic case. A's honest answer that the baby gets citizenship and parentage anyway let B establish that PRO's enforcement is friction, not deterrence, so the uncertified lane stays open while the state's stamp legitimates the whole trade — the framing that carried B's closing.</best_rebuttal>
